newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco mayor proposes $3.4 bln budget.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco mayor proposes $3.4 bln budget.

text.p: San Francisco Mayor Willie Brown on Monday proposed a $3.4 billion budget for fiscal year 1997-1998, promising to boost funding for public safety and health care programs.
Brown put to rest fears his spending plan would leave some city departments short of funds, saying "no layoffs, no cuts and no tax increases" would result from his budget.

"This budget proposes to have a healthier city, a cleaner city ... and, above all else, a very, very safe one," Brown said. "You'll find new monies to keep the streets cleaner, and we'll be investing our attention to graffiti."
Brown presented his $3.4 billion budget to the San Francisco Board of Supervisors, which will review the plan. The city's current fiscal year budget totals about $3.2 billion.
